edges.rationale: The edge section details how end systems (hosts) connect to the network; the basic notions of end systems and communication links must be introduced first.
The core section examines the mesh of packet switches and links and the ISP structure of the Internet, all of which are first defined in the overview of what the Internet is.
The quantitative delay model (especially transmission delay and queuing) presupposes store-and-forward packet switching and statistical multiplexing covered in the core.
The layered architecture and per-layer service model build directly on the definition of a protocol and the idea that all Internet communication is protocol-governed.
Attacks like packet sniffing and IP spoofing only make sense once the student knows what packets are and how protocols govern their exchange.
